The correct answer is C, a pulmonary shunt.  The reason is that the patient is showing no signs of improvement with oxygen therapy. This would not be expected from type 1 respiratory failure, but would be expected from type 2 respiratory failure, of which there are 3 causes: pulmonary shunt, hypoventilation and diffusion impairment.  Of the 3 causes of type 2 respiratory failure, only a pulmonary shunt would not be expected to improve with oxygen therapy.  Therefore the answer is C.  A pulmonary shunt is where blood passes through the lungs without coming into contact with the alveoli, so this would mean that the blood stays poorly oxygenated.  Hypoventilation is where there is inadequate ventilation of the alveoli, so the blood does come into contact with the alveoli and is therefore still able to be oxygenated. Diffusion impairment is where the diffusion of oxygen across the alveoli is impaired, but the blood still comes into contact with the alveoli and is therefore still able to be oxygenated.  A - low PiO2 is the result of type 1 respiratory failure, and therefore the wrong answer.  B - VQ mismatch is a cause of type 1 respiratory failure, and therefore the wrong answer.
